problem:
Given that ${y}_{0}(x)=\frac{2}{x}$ is a particular solution of the Riccati differential equation

$$
{y}^{′}={y}^{2}-\frac{4}{x}y+\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}
$$

 

find the general solution of the equation.
worked_solution:
The equation

$$
{y}^{′}={y}^{2}-\frac{4}{x}y+\frac{2}{{x}^{2}},
$$

is a Riccati differential equation of the form

$$
{y}^{′}=a(x){y}^{2}+b(x)y+c(x),
$$

where

$$
a(x)=1,\,b(x)=-\frac{4}{x},\,c(x)=\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}.
$$

To reduce the given Riccati equation to a Bernoulli equation, we use the substitution

$$
y(x)=z(x)+{y}_{0}(x),
$$

where ${y}_{0}(x)$ is a known particular solution.
Differentiating gives

$$
{y}^{′}(x)={z}^{′}(x)+{y}_{0}^{′}(x).
$$

In our case, ${y}_{0}(x)=\frac{2}{x}.$ Since ${y}_{0}^{′}(x)=-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}$, we have

$$
y=z+\frac{2}{x}\,⇒\,{y}^{′}={z}^{′}-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}.
$$

Let's substitute these expressions into our Riccati equation:

$$
{z}^{′}-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}=(z+\frac{2}{x})^{2}-\frac{4}{x}(z+\frac{2}{x})+\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}
$$

Now, we expand the right-hand side, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{′}-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}} & =({z}^{2}+\frac{4z}{x}+\frac{4}{{x}^{2}})-(\frac{4z}{x}+\frac{8}{{x}^{2}})+\frac{2}{{x}^{2}} \\ {z}^{′}-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}} & ={z}^{2}-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}} \\ {z}^{′} & ={z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve the obtained equation using separation of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & ={z}^{2} \\ \frac{1}{{z}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =1 \\ \int \frac{1}{{z}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \,\text{d}x \\ \int {z}^{-2}\,\text{d}z & =\int \text{d}x \\ -\frac{1}{z} & =x+C \\ z & =-\frac{1}{x+C}\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

Finally, let's substitute $z=y-\frac{2}{x}$ to recover the initial variable $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =-\frac{1}{x+C} \\ y-\frac{2}{x} & =-\frac{1}{x+C} \\ y & =-\frac{1}{x+C}+\frac{2}{x} \\  & =\frac{2}{x}-\frac{1}{x+C}\end{aligned}
$$
